alignments.note: δέ rendered by the verse-opening And.
Genitive absolute whose subject Ὀψίας is expressed, so the participle keeps the supplied subordinator, the copula and its own verb under rule 74.
Expressed subject of the absolute takes the English subject word.
Finite verb with its English subject; head on the lexical verb under rules 9 and 17.
Dative governed by the compound verb; the ASV writes a verb word of its own for the compound, so the preposition realizing the case rides with the pronoun under rules 21 and 106.
πολλούς rendered many; split from the participle under rule 26.

δαιμονίζομαι is a denominal -ίζω verb formed on δαίμων, so the supplied possessed answers to no element of it while demons is the root gloss. Rules 66, 91 and 104 head such a unit on the root word — ξενίζω → think it strange on strange, φλογίζω → setteth on fire on fire — and this chapter reads the same shape that way at 8:6 and 8:14, heading sick of the palsy on palsy and sick of a fever on fever. Heading on possessed remains defensible.
Compound verb with its English subject; the preverb ἐκ- is realized by out inside the unit under rule 106, headed on the verb word.
Anarthrous dative rendered with a word; the preposition realizes the case and the supplied determiner is a rule 51 helper.
πάντας has already written the one English word standing for the quantifier–article pair, so nothing is left for the substantival article to supply and it is unrepresented under rules 32 and 80.
Participle keeps the supplied relativizer and the copula of the English clause under rule 32.
Adverb κακῶς rendered by the predicate adjective sick; joining the pair as one light-verb unit under rule 73 remains defensible.

review_notes: Corrected the head of δαιμονιζομένους from possessed to demons: the lexeme is a denominal -ίζω verb on δαίμων, so its root gloss takes the head under rules 66, 91 and 104, matching this chapter's own sick of the palsy and sick of a fever units.
All other units left as accepted; all 18 source and 28 target IDs partitioned exactly once.
